voiceProfiles.styleNotes: Direct, short sentences, leads with the number that matters.
Warm but concrete, always names a specific detail about the company.
Founder-to-founder tone, references the product's workflow specifically.

stageAQuestions.title: Competitive dynamics
stageAQuestions.prompt: Is there a dominant player that owns the majority of the addressable market, or is the space fragmented across many providers? If dominant, name them and describe where the seams are.

stageAQuestions.title: Customer segmentation
stageAQuestions.prompt: Which segments in this category primarily serve SMB and mid-market customers, and which serve enterprise? Be specific about what those terms mean in this vertical.

stageAQuestions.title: Workflow product quality
stageAQuestions.prompt: Are the leading providers strong workflow products that generate proprietary data through daily use, or are they reporting layers and point tools that could be replaced without disrupting the core workflow?

stageAQuestions.title: Exit landscape
stageAQuestions.prompt: What does strategic acquisition and investment activity look like in this space? Who has been buying, and at what multiples?

judgmentSignals.signal: founder has domain background, built the product to solve their own problem
breakeven or profitable, high cash flow quality
founders own at least 50% of the company
primary distribution is direct, not via channel
product is a daily-use system of record, not a reporting layer
multi-party data exchange, platform serves more than one stakeholder type
regulatory or compliance complexity in the workflow

redFlags.signal: bad product or customer service signals from review sites
platform dependency on a single counterparty API or marketplace
channel concentration, all leads from one referral partner
market too crowded or too niche to support a platform thesis

specialists.question: Revenue quality, margin structure, and cash flow durability.
Overall commercial health: pipeline, pricing, customer mix.
